paper_title: Lattice QCD input for axion cosmology
suggested_experiment_name: Lattice QCD axion cosmology (pure-glue topological susceptibility, DIGM fit)
coupling_convention: y-values are T_1/T_c (dimensionless ratio of the axion oscillation-onset temperature to the QCD/pure-glue critical temperature) exactly as plotted in Fig. 9; x-values are f_a in GeV. This is NOT m_a; no conversion was applied per the plotted-values contract.
notes: First-principles lattice (pure SU(3) Yang-Mills, no dynamical fermions) calculation of the temperature-dependent topological susceptibility, used with the misalignment mechanism and the Planck dark-matter overclosure bound (Omega_DM h^2 = 0.1199 +/- 0.0027) to derive f_a <= (4.10 +/- 0.04) x 10^11 GeV, equivalently m_a >= (14.6 +/- 0.1) micro-eV, for post-inflation PQ breaking. This is a cosmological/theoretical bound on the f_a - m_a plane, hence AxionMass; it is NOT a haloscope DM-density-dependent limit, so dm_density_assumed is null. Note this is a lower bound on m_a (upper bound on f_a), excluding f_a > 4.10e11 GeV. Quoted uncertainties are 1-sigma statistical+systematic, not a formal 90/95% CL; confidence_level of 0.95 is nominal. Authors caveat that the pure-glue calculation carries uncontrolled systematics relative to full QCD (a proof-of-concept), and the bound includes only misalignment production (string/domain-wall decay would tighten it). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.45, 41)) | Vision: None of the figures on these pages is a true exclusion-limit plot in the (f_a, m_a) or (m_a, coupling) plane. The calibrated plot (Fig. 9, fig_03.png) shows T_1/T_c vs f_a [GeV] with linear y-axis 0-45, matching the provided calibration; I traced the solid black T_1 curve (dashed green benchmark is Wantz & Shellard). The paper's actual cosmological bound is a single constraint from Eq. 39: f_a <= (4.10+-0.04)e11 GeV, equivalently m_a >= (14.6+-0.1) micro-eV = 1.46e-5 eV, assuming Omega_a h^2 <= 0.1199 (PLANCK) in the post-inflation PQ-breaking scenario. Coupling type is AxionMass per the paper's f_a-m_a framing, but since the plotted y-quantity is T_1/T_c rather than m_a, extraction confidence is set below 0.5.
